name: Sell 3D-printable STL models on Cults3D, Printables Store and Thangs
summary: Design functional or decorative 3D-printable models and sell the files per download on 3D-printing marketplaces such as Cults3D, Printables and Thangs (roughly 20% fee).
howItWorks: You model and test-print functional or decorative objects (organisers, mounts, cosplay parts, replacement parts) and list STL/3MF files; hobbyists buy and print at home. Cults3D reportedly pays designers 80% of the sale; Printables Store charges a 20% fee (min. price $5, Stripe payouts); Thangs takes 30%/20%/15% for items under $5/$5-10/$10+ plus Stripe fees. Alternative: Bambu Lab's MakerWorld is free-download only, but models enrolled in its Exclusive Model Program earn Exclusive Points worth $0.066 each that can be cashed out per $100 earned (eligibility after 100 total prints on your account). Free uploads build followers who buy paid models; parametric OpenSCAD designs yield many variants.

methods: MakerWorld: Exclusive Points cash withdrawal -> bank (via payout provider; users report Airwallex wire)
payout.minimumPayout: Cults3D: threshold exists but amount unverified; Printables/Thangs: none stated (Stripe); MakerWorld: $100 of Exclusive Points per withdrawal
payout.frequency: Cults3D on request (unverified); Thangs monthly; Printables per Stripe schedule; MakerWorld on request (manual review ~1 week)
payout.notes: Thangs fees and Stripe-only payout confirmed on its help center (Stripe payout fee 0.25% + $0.25, currency conversion 2% non-US). Printables 20% fee / $5 minimum price confirmed on Prusa blog. MakerWorld cash rules confirmed on Bambu Lab blog (Oct 2024); regular MakerWorld points are NOT cash (points store only), and Printables Prusameters are NOT cash. Cults3D share/minimum/methods unverified (site returns 403).

legality.notes: Selling original 3D designs is legal everywhere; do not sell files of trademarked characters or replicas of copyrighted products; weapons files are prohibited by platforms and illegal in some countries.

availability.notes: Thangs payouts limited to its Stripe country list (~21/50 reference countries incl. US, UK, Canada, EU members, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Mexico, Argentina, Morocco, Singapore). Printables pays only via Stripe (limited list). Cults3D reportedly pays via PayPal (45/50 reference countries, unverified). MakerWorld cash-outs go to a bank account via its payout provider (country coverage unverified).

automationPlan: LLM drafts listings and print settings
Cross-post to all stores (MakerWorld exclusives cannot be sold elsewhere under the exclusive licence)
manualSteps: Physical test print of each model (needs access to a 3D printer)
risks: Untested AI-generated meshes fail to print and draw refunds
evidence: Prusa's Dec-2023 blog post documents the Printables Store (20% fee, Stripe, $5 min price). Thangs help center publishes its fee tiers and Stripe country list. Bambu Lab's Oct-2024 blog documents MakerWorld Exclusive Points cash rewards ($0.066/point, per $100). Cults3D's 80% designer share is reported by press (Fabbaloo) but its payout page could not be fetched.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $6 functional/decorative model; ~20% platform fee (Thangs charges 20% on $5-9.99 sales, 30% under $5, 15% at $10+; Cults3D/Printables similar) plus ~$0.50 card processing (estimated).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Printer ownership keeps growing (Bambu Lab), but MakerWorld and Printables' free-download culture means most users never pay; designers with followings sell paid files and earn from MakerWorld points. Text-to-3D AI is not yet good enough for functional parts, so craft still matters.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Give away several useful free models to build followers, price paid models at $3-8 and bundles at $15-25.
profitPath: Month 0: design and test-print 5 free + 3 paid models (filament ~$10)
Month 1-3: post free models, first paid sales

name: Monthly STL subscription for tabletop miniatures (Thangs Memberships, MyMiniFactory Tribes, Printables Clubs)
summary: Release a themed set of printable miniatures every month to paying subscribers on 3D-printing-native membership platforms.
howItWorks: Tabletop gamers with resin printers subscribe ($5-15/month) for a monthly release of pre-supported miniatures and terrain. Thangs Memberships charges a 14% platform fee (+Stripe fees); Printables Clubs launched with a 10% fee and Stripe payments (tiers $3-100); MyMiniFactory Tribes earnings are withdrawn via PayPal on the 14th/28th. Unlike generic Patreon, files are delivered automatically to a 3D-print search audience. Back-catalogue sets are later sold as bundles.

methods: MyMiniFactory: payout request -> PayPal (14th and 28th for Pro/Studio; 28th only for Upcoming) or bank transfer (monthly, 28th)
payout.minimumPayout: No minimum stated by Thangs, Printables or MyMiniFactory; MyMiniFactory charges a $2 processing fee on payouts under $100
payout.frequency: Thangs monthly; MyMiniFactory twice-monthly on request; Printables via Stripe
payout.notes: MyMiniFactory Tribes requires the Pro ($24.99/mo) or Studio ($99.99/mo) creator plan (store commission 15/12.5/10% by tier + 3.49% + $0.49 processing); the Tribes-specific commission is not published on the creator help center. Thangs membership fee 14% and Printables Clubs 10% confirmed on official pages.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; sculpts must be original (no Games Workshop/Disney likenesses).

availability.notes: MyMiniFactory pays by PayPal (45/50 reference countries) or bank; Thangs memberships limited to its Stripe country list (~21/50 reference countries); Printables Clubs via Stripe (limited country list).

automationPlan: Blender batch renders for promo images
Scheduled monthly release posts and Discord announcements
LLM writes lore/stat cards per release
manualSteps: Sculpting each month's set (ZBrush/Blender) - heavy manual art work
risks: Monthly content treadmill; churn when releases slip
Paid MMF tier is a fixed cost (Pro $24.99/mo; the $0 monthly cost here assumes Thangs or Printables Clubs)
evidence: MyMiniFactory creator help center documents payout schedule, $2 fee under $100 and store fees; Thangs help center publishes the 14% membership fee and supported countries; Prusa blog announced Clubs with a 10% fee. Dozens of mini studios run 4-5 figure monthly subscriptions.

tools: Lychee or Chitubox (free tiers) for pre-supporting

unitEconomics.notes: Median $10/month tier; Thangs 14% fee plus ~$0.60 Stripe processing. Each monthly release is a fixed ~60-80 hours of work regardless of subscriber count.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Established sculptors with recognisable styles and back-catalogues earn thousands monthly; newcomers struggle to get the first 20 subscribers. The workload is a monthly treadmill, and piracy of STL packs is common. AI sculpting still falls short of print-ready minis.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $5-7 with a generous first release, then add a $10-15 tier with commercial-print licences.
profitPath: Month 0-2: sculpt a 6-10 model launch release (cost $0)
Month 3-6: monthly releases, free samples; 10-40 subscribers
Month 6-12: median ~$70/month net; churn is the main risk

name: Craft design files on Creative Fabrica, Design Bundles and So Fontsy
summary: Upload SVG cut files, laser-cut templates, embroidery files and craft fonts to craft marketplaces that also pay from all-access subscriptions.
howItWorks: Cricut/Silhouette/laser and embroidery hobbyists buy files individually or via all-access subscriptions. Designers are paid per individual sale plus a share of the subscription pool weighted by downloads, so a large catalogue earns small recurring amounts. Unlike Etsy you pay no listing fees and the marketplace brings its own traffic. Bundle deals and freebies feature designers to new buyers.

payout.notes: Revenue-share percentages, subscription-pool formula and minimum payouts still unverified: Creative Fabrica (site and help center), Design Bundles and So Fontsy all returned 403/429 to fetches in Nov 2026; commonly reported ~50% share of individual sales.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; do not upload licensed characters/brand logos; AI-generated designs must follow each marketplace's disclosure policy.

availability.notes: PayPal/Payoneer payouts reach most reference countries (Payoneer 50/50, PayPal 45/50).

automationPlan: Generate and vectorise designs in batches (AI + Inkscape trace)
Scripted export to SVG/DXF/PNG/EPS bundle formats
manualSteps: Manual quality check that paths cut cleanly
risks: Subscription pool payouts are tiny per download
Flooding by AI designs depresses earnings
evidence: Creative Fabrica and Design Bundles host tens of thousands of independent designers; payouts are widely documented by crafter-designers but terms were not verifiable here.

tools: AI image tools for ideation (check marketplace AI rules)
Creative Fabrica / Design Bundles designer accounts
skills: SVG design clean enough for cutting machines

unitEconomics.notes: Median $3 cut file; designer share ~50% is estimated (Creative Fabrica and Design Bundles pages bot-blocked). Subscription-pool earnings per download are a few cents and not modelled.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Large-catalogue designers (thousands of files) earn steady pool income; small shops earn cents per download. Marketplaces and buyers are flooded with AI SVGs, and Creative Fabrica pushes its own AI tools.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Accept marketplace default pricing; drive individual sales via free items and bundle-deal participation.

name: Licensed artist for cutting-machine design stores (Silhouette Design Store)
summary: Become an approved artist whose cut files are sold inside the machine maker's own design store and software, chiefly the Silhouette Design Store in Silhouette Studio (most designs sell at $0.99; royalty rate unpublished).
howItWorks: Silhouette's Design Store sells cut files directly inside Silhouette Studio, which every Silhouette Cameo/Portrait owner uses. Approved artists (500+ listed) upload original designs; the store pays royalties per purchase/subscription use. Silhouette also advertises an open 'Marketplace Shop' where registered sellers list products. This reaches buyers at the point of cutting, unlike Etsy. Similar license deals exist with Cricut's Design Space image library on a contract basis.

payout.notes: Royalty rate, payout method and minimum are not published: the become-an-artist, artist-application, register-as-an-artists and marketplace pages (checked Nov 2026) show only sign-up links. Cricut artist licensing terms are private contracts.

availability.notes: Store is global; payout rail unverified.

risks: Dependence on a single device ecosystem
evidence: Silhouette Design Store publicly lists 500+ artists and an artist application page.

unitEconomics.notes: Most Silhouette designs sell at $0.99; the artist royalty share is not published - ~30% is estimated (the become-an-artist page gives no figure).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Long-standing approved artists with large catalogues get featured; newcomers face approval delays and opaque royalty terms. AI-made vector art increases competition; price points are fixed by the store.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Prices are largely fixed by the store ($0.99 typical), so compete on volume, seasonal sets and being featured; use the open Marketplace Shop for higher-priced bundles.

name: Knitting and crochet pattern sales on Ravelry, LoveCrafts and Ribblr
summary: Design, test-knit and sell written knitting/crochet patterns on yarn-community marketplaces such as Ravelry (buyers pay your PayPal directly) and Ribblr (Stripe, fee from 4%).
howItWorks: You design a garment or amigurumi, write the sized pattern with charts, run test knitters and sell the PDF. On Ravelry buyers pay your PayPal directly; Ravelry bills a small monthly fee (reportedly none under $30/month in sales, ~3.5% above). LoveCrafts runs an indie designer program. Ribblr sells interactive ePatterns via Stripe Connect with a sale fee from 4% (reducible to 0% with its '$elFee' scheme, min. fee $0.25 per pattern). Patterns indexed in Ravelry's project database sell for years.

methods: Ravelry: buyer pays your PayPal directly -> bank
payout.minimumPayout: Ravelry: none (instant to PayPal); Ribblr: none stated (Stripe); LoveCrafts unverified
payout.frequency: instant (Ravelry, Ribblr per Stripe); monthly (LoveCrafts, unverified)
payout.notes: Ribblr fees and Stripe Connect requirement confirmed in its Payments Policy. Ravelry fee figures come from designer blogs (fee table is behind login; help pages return login/500). LoveCrafts designer handbook returned 429; share unverified.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; patterns are copyrightable instructions; avoid copying others' charts.
complianceRequirements: EU VAT handled per platform rules

availability.notes: Ravelry requires PayPal (receivable in 45/50 reference countries; not Nigeria, Lebanon, Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq). Ribblr requires a Stripe account (limited country list).

automationPlan: Chart generation (Stitch Fiddle) and PDF layout templates
LLM drafts pattern text and listing copy for review
fullCycle: Open Ravelry designer store and PayPal
risks: Errors in patterns cause refunds/bad reputation
AI cannot reliably write correct patterns
evidence: Ravelry hosts over a million patterns with thousands of paid indie designers; pattern-sales platform comparisons document its PayPal-based model.

tools: free charting tools (Stitch Fiddle) and Google Docs/Canva for layout
skills: original knit/crochet design and grading sizes
equipment: yarn and tools (sample yarn ~$20-60 per design, assumed from stash or yarn support)

unitEconomics.notes: Median $7 PDF pattern; Ravelry ~3.5% above $30/month in sales plus PayPal ~3.49% + $0.49 (~$0.73).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale. Sample yarn is excluded (assumed stash).

marketConditions.notes: Designers with consistent style and Instagram/YouTube presence sell well; Ravelry's database keeps patterns selling for years. AI cannot reliably produce working patterns, and 2024-2025 scandals over fake AI crochet patterns increased buyer trust in tested human designs.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch new patterns at a 20-30% discount for a week, then standard $6-9; sell e-book collections at $20-30.
profitPath: Month 0-1: design, knit and test 1-2 patterns (cost $0-40)
Month 1-3: release with launch discount; first sales

name: PDF sewing and quilting patterns with projector files (Etsy, Payhip, Makerist)
summary: Draft, grade and sell multi-size sewing and quilting patterns as print-at-home, A0 copy-shop and projector files via Payhip (5% fee on the free plan) or Etsy.
howItWorks: Home sewists buy PDF patterns that include tiled A4/Letter pages, A0 copy-shop files, layered sizes and projector files, plus an illustrated instruction booklet. Quilters buy block/quilt patterns with fabric requirements and cutting charts. Etsy and Payhip handle direct sales (Payhip free plan: 5% fee, sales deposited instantly to your PayPal/Stripe). Makerist, a European pattern marketplace, appeared offline in Nov 2026. Pattern testers and sew-along posts drive launches; one pattern sells for years.

payout.minimumPayout: Payhip: none (instant); Etsy per Etsy Payments schedule; Makerist unverified
payout.notes: Payhip fees confirmed on its pricing page: Free 5%, Plus $29/mo 2%, Pro $99/mo 0%, plus PayPal/Stripe fees. Makerist status: in Nov 2026 makerist.com had no DNS address, makerist.de served an expired TLS certificate and other country domains failed TLS - the marketplace appears offline/closed (no official notice found); do not rely on it.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; pattern drafting from scratch only (no tracing commercial patterns).
complianceRequirements: EU VAT on digital goods (Payhip/Etsy collect)

availability.notes: Payhip (PayPal or Stripe) and Etsy pay in most reference countries; Makerist (EU-focused) appears offline.

automationPlan: LLM drafts instruction text; diagram templates reused
risks: Competition from big indie pattern houses
evidence: Indie pattern houses (e.g. many on Etsy, and formerly Makerist, which appears offline since Nov 2026) sell PDF patterns as primary business; projector files became standard after 2020.

tools: Inkscape (free) or Seamly2D (free) for pattern drafting

unitEconomics.notes: Median $14 PDF pattern; Payhip free plan 5% plus ~$0.72 PayPal/Stripe processing.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Indie designers with sew-along communities and testers succeed; patterns sell for years. AI cannot yet produce graded, tested patterns reliably, so competition is mostly human. Development is slow and fit problems cause refunds.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch with a time-limited discount for testers' followers, then $12-16; sell size bundles and quilt kits at higher prices.
profitPath: Month 0-2: develop and test one pattern (cost $0-40)

name: Cross-stitch charts and machine-embroidery files
summary: Sell cross-stitch charts (PDF + Pattern Keeper-compatible) and machine-embroidery files (PES/DST/JEF) for hobbyists.
howItWorks: Cross-stitchers buy charts with colour keys (DMC) that work in the Pattern Keeper app; embroidery-machine owners buy multi-format stitch files plus colour sheets. Charts are generated from original artwork with stitch software and hand-cleaned; machine designs are digitised in free Ink/Stitch (Inkscape) or paid Hatch/Embrilliance. Sold on Payhip or Etsy (about 5-7% fees, the basis of the unit economics) and on Creative Fabrica and LoveCrafts (cross-stitch; shares unverified); bundles of themed seasonal designs sell repeatedly each year.

payout.notes: Payhip terms confirmed (5% fee on free plan, instant PayPal/Stripe deposit). Creative Fabrica and LoveCrafts shares/minimums unverified (pages return 403/429).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; do not chart licensed characters or others' art without permission.

availability.notes: Payhip/Payoneer cover nearly all reference countries.

automationPlan: Image-to-chart pipeline (original art -> colour-reduced DMC chart)
evidence: Creative Fabrica and LoveCrafts list thousands of independent embroidery and cross-stitch designs; Pattern Keeper compatibility is a common selling point.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $6 chart; blended Payhip/Etsy fees ~7% + ~$0.50 processing.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Designers with original art and Pattern Keeper-compatible PDFs sell steadily, especially seasonal sets. Auto-charted AI images have flooded Etsy and lowered trust and prices.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price single charts at $4-7, seasonal bundles at $12-20.
profitPath: Month 1-3: list on Payhip/Etsy; first sales

name: Sell LEGO MOC building instructions on Rebrickable
summary: Design original LEGO models (MOCs) and sell PDF instructions plus parts lists as Premium MOCs on Rebrickable; buyers source the bricks themselves.
howItWorks: You build a model digitally in BrickLink Studio (free), generate step-by-step instructions, and list it as a Premium MOC on Rebrickable. Buyers pay for the instructions and use Rebrickable to buy parts or match their own collection. Payment goes straight to your PayPal or Stripe account; Rebrickable then deducts or invoices its commission (reported 8%/13%/18% by price band on its Designer Plan). Popular MOC designers also get approached by kit sellers for licensing.

payout.minimumPayout: None (paid at time of sale); commission invoiced monthly when owed > $5
payout.notes: Commission tiers and $5 invoice threshold from Rebrickable help pages seen via search snippets; live help/plans pages returned 403 to fetches in Nov 2026, so still unverified.

legality.notes: Legal: MOC instructions are your own work; LEGO's fan policy allows it, but do not use LEGO logos or sell counterfeit kits.

availability.notes: PayPal works in 45/50 reference countries; users report PayPal/Stripe issues in some (e.g. Ukraine, South Korea).

automationPlan: Studio auto-generates instruction steps and parts lists
risks: Copying of MOCs by kit makers
evidence: Rebrickable's founder interview and help pages describe the Premium MOC marketplace where designers sell instructions.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $12 MOC; Rebrickable commission ~13% at that band (estimated; Rebrickable fee page bot-blocked), plus PayPal ~3.49% + $0.49.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Adult LEGO fans are a growing market; designers with recognisable themes (modulars, vehicles) and good renders sell repeatedly. Kit cloners copying popular MOCs are a risk.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $8-12, raise to $15-25 for large builds; offer alternate builds of popular official sets.
profitPath: Month 1-3: list as Premium MOCs; first sales

name: Tabletop RPG adventures and supplements on DMs Guild / DriveThruRPG
summary: Write and sell PDF adventures, monsters, maps and rules supplements for D&D and other RPGs on OneBookShelf marketplaces.
howItWorks: On DMs Guild you may use official D&D IP (Forgotten Realms etc.) under the Community Content Program and earn a reported 50% royalty. On DriveThruRPG you sell your own-IP or 5e-SRD (CC-BY) products for a higher reported share. Customers are GMs looking for ready-to-run content; bestseller medals (Copper/Silver/etc.) drive visibility. Bundles and print-on-demand versions add revenue. Text must be human-written: the marketplaces do not accept products written primarily by AI.

payout.notes: 50% DMs Guild split confirmed only via press/creator sources; DriveThruRPG royalty (creator comments cite 65% non-exclusive / 70% exclusive) and payout rules unverified (dmsguild.com, drivethrurpg.com and its help center return 403). AI policy (per Gizmodo/EN World 2023 coverage): since 31 Jul 2023 products made primarily of AI-written text are not accepted, standalone AI-art products are barred and AI-generated art must be labelled; buyers can filter 'Handcrafted' vs 'Contains AI'. Community programs (DMs Guild, Chaosium's Miskatonic Repository) set their own stricter rules - Chaosium removed 40+ community titles over AI text in Oct 2026.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; DMs Guild content is licensed IP that must stay on DMs Guild; follow OGL/CC rules on DriveThruRPG.

availability.notes: OneBookShelf sells globally; PayPal reaches 45/50 reference countries.

automationPlan: LLM for brainstorming, proofreading and consistency checks only (text must be human-written; disclose any AI use)
Map generation tools (label AI art or use licensed/hand-made art)
risks: IP licence terms controlled by Wizards of the Coast
evidence: DMs Guild launched 2016 with a 50/50 split reported by Kotaku and others; many creators publish sales reports. aiLeverage lowered to 3 because the marketplaces bar primarily AI-written products.

tools: free stock art from publishers' art packs

unitEconomics.notes: Median $5 adventure; DMs Guild pays 50% royalty, DriveThruRPG ~65-70% for own IP (estimated, from reports).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Prolific creators with series and bestseller medals earn most; most titles sell under 50 copies. AI-written text is banned, keeping human competition, while the 2024 D&D rules refresh brought new demand.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Release a pay-what-you-want title to build an audience, then price adventures at $3-8 and bundles at $15-25.
profitPath: Month 0: write and lay out first adventure (cost $0)

name: Publish print-on-demand board and card games on The Game Crafter
summary: Upload a board/card game design; The Game Crafter prints and ships each order and pays you 70% of the markup.
howItWorks: You design a card or board game, upload art files, set a retail price above TGC's manufacturing cost, and list it in their shop. TGC manufactures and ships each copy (physical step done by the platform, not you). Royalty = 70% of (price - cost); e.g. $15 price - $8 cost = $7 profit, you get $4.90. Payouts run every Monday after a 30-day hold. Contests on TGC and print-and-play versions help gain traction.

payout.notes: Royalties default to shop credit unless a valid PayPal email is set. Publishing requires buying a copy of your own game and waiting 10 days (contest entries exempt).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; avoid gambling mechanics and licensed IP.

availability.notes: PayPal payout reaches 45/50 reference countries. Physical product is printed/shipped by TGC (marked PHYSICAL but no seller handling).

automationPlan: AI-assisted card art and rules drafting
Scripted card generation from spreadsheets (e.g. nanDECK)
manualSteps: Ordering one physical copy of your game (required before publishing to the shop, then a 10-day wait)
evidence: TGC help center documents 70/30 profit split, weekly payouts and PayPal method.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $20 game with ~$10 manufacturing cost; TGC keeps 30% of the ~$10 profit (= 15% of price), you get ~$7. TGC's 70/30 profit split confirmed on its royalties help page.

breakEven.notes: Startup $30 = proof copy. Month-6 net ~$10 means ~3 months to recover.

marketConditions.notes: Few print-on-demand games sell more than a handful of copies; designers who win TGC contests or build a community on BoardGameGeek and Reddit do best. Manufacturing and shipping costs rose in 2025-2026, squeezing a margin that is already ~$7 on a $20 game. AI art lowers production cost but does not solve discovery.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price just above manufacturing cost plus a small margin to win early buyers and contest votes; raise price once reviews arrive, and offer a free print-and-play version as a funnel.

name: Virtual tabletop assets and modules (Roll20 Marketplace, Foundry VTT premium modules)
summary: Sell battle maps, tokens and ready-to-run modules for virtual tabletops on the Roll20 Marketplace, Foundry VTT's Marketplace (opened Feb 2025) or your own store. Maps are built in Dungeondraft/Wonderdraft from reusable asset packs.
howItWorks: Online RPG groups pay for tokens, battle maps, character sheets and automated modules. Roll20 Marketplace sells creator art packs and adventures with a revenue share. Foundry VTT opened its own official Marketplace on 12 Feb 2025; creators can also sell premium modules via their own store (activation keys) or Patreon-linked access. Battle maps can be produced in Dungeondraft/Wonderdraft with consistent asset packs.

methods: Own store via Stripe/PayPal or Patreon
payout.notes: Roll20 revenue share and payout rules not verifiable: help center returns 403 and the 'Become a Creator' page linked from marketplace.roll20.net (pages.roll20.net/marketplace-creators) returned 404 in Nov 2026. Foundry Marketplace creator terms are not public.

automationPlan: Batch map generation with templated asset packs
evidence: Roll20 Marketplace has hosted community creators for years; Foundry premium module ecosystem is well established.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $10 map/token pack; Roll20 creator share estimated at 50% (Roll20 help and wiki pages bot-blocked, unverified).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Battlemap and token creators who already run Patreon audiences dominate sales; Foundry VTT's official Marketplace (2025) and continued online play support demand. AI-generated battlemaps flooded the market in 2024-2026, pushing pack prices down, and Roll20's creator revenue share is not published (50% assumed). Typical failure mode: packs listed with no audience get almost no marketplace visibility.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Give away a free sample pack to build followers, price map/token packs at $5-15 and offer $25-30 bundles; add premium Foundry modules with automation at higher prices.
